key: E’en with the weak he wrought this matchless exploit: e’en with a goat he did to death a lion. He pared the pillar’s angles with a needle.
s: Late in a hymn on Indra’s aid to Sudas in battle, the verse names three marvels; Sāyaṇa, on 7.18.17, takes the weak one as Sudas when poor, and holds the three deeds not to be doubted as impossible, since Indra’s greatness surpasses them.

evidence.gloss: Indra then, even through Sudās when poor (ādhra glossed as daridra), caused one chief act of giving to be done. Even an aged lion he had slain by a goat. With a needle he cut the corners of the sacrificial post and the like: the needle did the work of an adze. These three deeds are not to be doubted as impossible, because of the surpassing greatness of Indra.
